title: Math & Excel Review

learningObjectives.text: Know and understand the following mathematical concepts: function, slope, derivative, power rule, partial derivative
Know and understand how to use calculus to optimize managerial decisions

Know and understand how to do the following in Excel: create a scatterplot; adjust the horizontal and vertical axes to fit the range of the data; add a title and label the x- and y-axes; add a trendline to a plot; use Solver to optimize managerial decisions

keyTerms.def: A quantitative formula that defines the relationship between a set of inputs and outputs.
The rise over the run, or the change in y over the change in x (Δy/Δx). For y = mx + b, m is the slope and b is the intercept.

A function that evaluates the instantaneous rate of change of some original function, i.e., it tells you the slope (Δy/Δx) at any given value of x. For a straight line, the slope and derivative are equal; for a curve, it is the slope of the tangent line at that point.
keyTerms.src: Math Review p.5; S05 slides pp.19-20

keyTerms.def: For y = x^a, dy/dx = a·x^(a−1). Bring the exponent down in front and subtract 1 from the exponent; constants (no x) drop out.
keyTerms.src: Math Review p.5; S05 slides p.27

keyTerms.def: The derivative of a function with respect to one individual independent variable while the other variables are held constant. Written ∂y/∂x. Used to isolate the effect of specific variables.
keyTerms.src: Math Review p.10; S05 slides p.43
